summary: Donald Capps (1939–2015) was a scholar in religious studies who studied at Lewis & Clark College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held positions at Oregon State, Chicago, UNC Charlotte, Phillips University, and Princeton Theological Seminary (1981–2009).

Donald E. Gjertson (b. 1944) is a sinologist and scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford under John Ching-yu Wang, also studying under Akira Takeda, and held a post at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~1976–2012).

Donald K. Swearer (b. 1934) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en and Singkha Wannasai. He held posts at Swarthmore College (~1970–2004), Chiang Mai University, and Harvard University (2004–2010).

Donald Keene (1922–2019) was a Japanologist who studied at Columbia University under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Harvard. He held academic posts at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University (1955).

Donald Phillip Verene (b. 1937) is a philosopher who studied at Knox College and earned his doctorate at Washington University in St. Louis. He served as Chair at Emory University (1982–1988) and held visiting appointments at Pembroke College and the University of Rome.

Donald R. Davis Jr. (b. 1970) is an indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Patrick Olivelle, Ludo Rocher, and Richard W. Lariviere. He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and on the Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies editorial board.

Donald S. Lopez, Jr. (b. 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his BA, MA, and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, held posts at Middlebury and Bristol, and joined the University of Michigan in 1990.

Donald Wiebe (b. 1943) is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He held a post at Trinity College, Toronto (~1980) and served as General Editor for Toronto Studies in Religion (attested 1996).
Dondub Buddhayin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who served as abbot at Chilttai Monastery and at Ganden Dargye Ling (attested 1933). He also taught Eugène Obermiller.

id: P:Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso
summary: Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Dongak Chokyi Nyima studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dongak Tendzin was a student of Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He also taught Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Dongchu (1908–1977) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Minnan Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He held positions at Dinghui Temple and Jiaoshan Buddhist Institute, and founded Humanity Magazine, Chung-Hwa Institute, and Nung Chan Monastery.

Dongmei Fang (1899–1977) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Nanking under John Dewey and earned an MA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He held posts at National Central University and National Taiwan University.

Donna C. Kurtz (b. 1943) is an archaeologist and historian who studied at the University of Cincinnati, Somerville College, Oxford, and Yale University. She held a post at the Classical Art Research Centre from approximately 1970 to 2011.

Dor Bahadur Bista (b. 1928) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies who studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus. He was a professor at Tribhuvan University (~1975–1990), founded the Karnali Institute, and served on the board of ICIMOD.
Doranne Jacobson (b. 1940) is an Indologist who completed a doctorate in anthropology at Columbia University, where she also held a post as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

Doris Meth Srinivasan is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Hunter College and the University of Pennsylvania, and held posts at George Mason University, Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Columbia, Barnard, George Washington, and Stony Brook University.
Doris Unterthurner is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Dorje Rinchen (1819–1867) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under Sakya Yab Jé Kün Ga Rinchen, Ja Shong Lob Zur Lodrö Gyatso, Nying Ri Tri Chen Tutob Tendzin, Chime Tenpai Nyima, and Sakya Dak Chen, and taught Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
